	The 60th annual CMA Awards show is being telecast live by ABC from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena. Scroll down to see the 2026 winners as they are named over the course of the three-hour show.

	Ella Langley is favored to win with many of her nine nominations. Indeed, she got off to a good start with the first award to be presented during the telecast, single of the year, which went as expected to “Choosin’ Texas.” The mammoth hit also won an award that was announced prior to the show, for video of the year.
	

	Lainey Wilson is hosting for the third year in a row, and surprised the audience by having former co-host Brad Paisley out to join her for the monologue, doing a medley of musical parodies, as Paisley used to do with Carrie Underwood when they shepherded the show.

	Following are the categories for the 2026 CMAs, with the winners put in bold as their names are announced:

title: Jason Blum and James Wan Discuss Why Horror Is Hollywood’s Hottest Genre and How ‘Obsession’ Hit Big at Blumhouse Atomic’s Business of Fear
description: Blumhouse Atomic bosses Jason Blum and James Wan took a victory lap Wednesday at their Business of Fear panel, during which they discussed horror’s
body:
Blumhouse Atomic bosses Jason Blum and James Wan took a victory lap Wednesday at their Business of Fear panel, during which they discussed horror’s banner year at the box office and why “Obsession” became the breakout hit of the summer. 

	But before the horror talk began, they had to address the name change. Blum’s Blumhouse and Wan’s Atomic Monster merged in 2024, and the combined labels were therefore known as Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Recently, in early November, Blumhouse Atomic Monster rebranded to just Blumhouse Atomic. Blum explained they rebranded to give a more definitive identity to the overarching banner of the two companies, while also clearing the way for both distinct labels to take credit for their work. 
	

	Wan added that Blumhouse Atomic Monster was also “a bit of a mouthful.” 

	“As Jason pointed out, it really still is Blumhouse movies and Atomic Monster movies,” Wan added. “We’re still making the movies as one company, but still under two labels. We put out a bunch of movies, and so we have to sort of divide it. Some movies play better at Atomic Monster, some movies play better at Blumhouse. At the start of movies, even though it’s going to say Blumhouse Atomic Presents, our logos will still stand individually.”

	It was then on to horror’s stellar year. Moderator Ray Subers, head of film at NRG, presented Blum and Wan with a stat that theater attendance for horror films in 2026 went up 7% from pre-pandemic levels, while attendance for all other genre films (action, sci-fi, rom-coms) decreased. Blum theorized this was because watching horror on the big screen is “participatory,” and that audiences craved a “collective experience” after emerging from COVID lockdown. 
	

	“I think that after COVID, audiences ran back to sporting events and ran back to concerts, but they had been fed movies,” Blum said. “Kids had been fed movies so much at home that it took longer to discover and remember the movies [in the theater]. And I think horror specifically, if there’s any genre that’s close to a concert or a sporting event, I think horror is more than anything else because it’s so participatory. I think movies generally, but horror specifically, are kind of joining sports and concerts as a great way to get out of your house and have a collective, fun, exciting thing to do that doesn’t involve your phone.” 

	The conversation then shifted to “Obsession.” Blum joined as an executive producer shortly after Focus Features acquired the film, which, from a budget of less than $1 million, grossed over $500 million worldwide. Blum said he thinks “Obsession” took off for two reasons. The first is because young people can relate to the “universal feeling” of being “obsessed or having someone obsessed with them.” The second reason was that director Curry Barker sharpened his filmmaking skills on YouTube and social media before coming to Hollywood. 

	“I think that he has a dialogue with his audience, which he has honed over years and years and years of putting little pieces of content on YouTube and watching his audience react and adjusting to it,” Blum said. “The best way I can describe it is it almost feels like when you’re watching the movie, Curry is like whispering in your ear little funny things or like you’re talking to this invisible hand that’s directing the movie in a way that’s very unique.” 

	Wan added that the success of “Obsession” has inspired a whole new generation of filmmakers wanting to make scary movies, which reminds him of when he was trying to break into the industry with “Saw.” 

	“That stigma is gone. Horror has crossed over from the black sheep of the household, right?” Wan said. “I really do credit the younger generation with accepting the genre in a big way and not turning your nose down on it in a snooty way. When I was doing ‘Saw’ people looked down on it, right? And it was only a certain demographic that would come out and support the films that we made. But today, like today, it is cool and hip to be making horror films.”

title: Bear Grylls, Dhar Mann, Erin Foster, Lonnie Ali, Cameron Alexander and Sonja Warfield to Be Honored at Variety’s Third Annual Faith & Spirituality in Entertainment Honors
description: Variety has announced its Faith and Spirituality in Entertainment Visionary Awards honorees who will be recognized at the third annual Faith and Sp
body:
Variety has announced its Faith and Spirituality in Entertainment Visionary Awards honorees who will be recognized at the third annual Faith and Spirituality in Entertainment Honors, presented by the Coalition for Faith & Media in Los Angeles, on Dec. 2.

	The Honors will celebrate individuals who are supporting often underrepresented themes of faith and spirituality across film and TV. The event coincides with Variety’s annual Faith & Media Impact Report, recognizing those who are championing belief-centered storytelling within the entertainment industry.
	

	The honorees for the evening include: Bear Grylls, two-time Emmy Award-winner and best-selling author; Dhar Mann, founder Dhar Mann Studios; Erin Foster, creator, “Nobody Wants This”; Lonnie Ali, executive producer of Muhammad Ali TV series “The Greatest”; Cameron Alexander, screenwriter, “Heart of the Beast”; and Sonja Warfield, the Emmy-nominated co-showrunner and executive producer for HBO’s highly awarded drama, “The Gilded Age.”

	Grylls is a former British Special Forces soldier, who became one of the youngest climbers to summit Mount Everest. He went on to host a string of hit adventure series, including Discovery Channel’s “Man vs. Wild” and “Running Wild With Bear Grylls,” now in its ninth season.

	Foster is a writer, actress, and producer best known for creating the acclaimed comedy series “Nobody Wants This,” an AFI Awards honoree nominated for Golden Globe, Emmy, and Critics Choice Awards. Under her Fatigue Sisters overall deal with 20th Television, she is currently developing the drama “These Summer Storms,” based on Sarah MacLean’s novel, for Hulu. Beyond television, Erin co-owns the fashion brand Favorite Daughter and co-hosts the award-winning “The World’s First Podcast.”
	

	Mann is an influential storyteller and founder of Dhar Mann Studios, an audience-first global entertainment company dedicated to uplifting audiences through stories and experiences that help people feel seen and connected. The studio reaches more than 170 million followers and generates over 320 million views each week across platforms.

	Ali is an executive producer on the upcoming Amazon biopic series “The Greatest” and the documentary, “The City of Ali.” She is also the creator and co-host of the award-winning podcast “Ali in Me” on Audible and will executive produce a planned documentary about the relationship between Muhammad Ali and legendary broadcaster Howard Cosell. She and her husband opened the Muhammad Ali Center in Louisville in November of 2005, where she serves as a lifetime director and vice chair of the board. The Muhammad Ali Center’s mission is to inspire greatness, cultivate curious and courageous leaders, and grow a more compassionate world.

	Cameron’s original feature screenplay, “Heart of the Beast,” is a survival thriller film starring Brad Pitt that was released in September this year. He recently wrote “Dreams in Antlered Moonlight,” which he will direct in his feature directorial debut.

	Warfield is a television writer, producer and author whose credits include her work on the Emmy Award-winning NBC sitcom “Will & Grace” as well as BET’s hit comedy “The Game.” Currently, she’s the Emmy-nominated executive producer and co-showrunner for HBO’s highly awarded drama, “The Gilded Age.”

	The night will feature award presentations to the honorees, alongside a networking reception and seated dinner, hosted by Rainn Wilson.

	Wilson is the Emmy-nominated and SAG award-winning actor best known for playing Dwight Schrute for nine seasons on “The Office.” He is also a New York Times best-selling author, whose latest book is entitled “The Soul Boom Workbook: Spiritual Tools for Modern Living.” He co-founded the digital media company SoulPancake and Lide Haiti, an arts and education non-profit in rural Haiti.

	“We are honored to partner with the Coalition for Faith & Media and Fetzer Institute to advance a meaningful conversation about the portrayal of faith and spirituality in media,” said Dea Lawrence, co-president and publisher of Variety. “Media plays a powerful role in shaping cultural understanding and influencing how we see one another. Creating greater awareness of the diverse ways faith and spirituality inform people’s lives is essential to fostering more authentic, nuanced and inclusive storytelling.”
	

	“More than three-quarters of the world identifies as religious, spiritual, or a person of faith,” said Brooke Zaugg, executive director, Coalition for Faith and Media. “Audiences want to see their values reflected in the stories they watch. It’s good business and a meaningful way to create greater understanding of those around us. We’re grateful for Variety’s leadership, honoring the diverse industry voices who are bringing faith to the screen in artful, nuanced, and entertaining ways.”

	Past honorees have included Mo Amer, Tiffany Haddish, Viola Davis, Sheryl Lee Ralph, Jay Shetty, and Julius Tennon.

title: Elon Musk Admits He Feels ‘Pretty Foolish’ Having Spent Nearly $500 Million on Midterm Election Races Won by Democrats, Claims He Is ‘Not MAGA’
description: Elon Musk spent big backing Republicans in the 2026 midterm elections — which resulted in a sweeping defeat of the GOP as Democrats took over the H
body:
Elon Musk spent big backing Republicans in the 2026 midterm elections — which resulted in a sweeping defeat of the GOP as Democrats took over the House and Senate.

	Musk spent nearly $500 million during the midterms, including $200 million to try to defeat Senator-elect James Talarico in Texas in his race against Lone Star State attorney general Ken Paxton.

	“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk conceded, “or maybe it would have been much worse without that.” Musk appeared virtually Wednesday at the New York Times’ 2026 DealBook Summit in New York City, connecting via videoconference from China, where the tech mogul is part of President Donald Trump’s American delegation to the region.
	

	Earlier at the conference, Skydance CEO David Ellison said Musk — whose roles include founder, CEO and chief engineer of SpaceX and CEO of Tesla — has become an investor in Skydance, the company formed through the megamerger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. “[T]o have him as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege,” Ellison said. (The subject of Skydance did not come up in Musk’s appearance.)

	On the topic of the midterms, Musk said he believes the newly elected Democratic governor of Texas, Gina Hinojosa, “I think is going to be quite moderate. I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor, and based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with [Hinojosa] as governor.”

	Musk, who ranks as the world’s wealthiest individual, insisted that “I’m not MAGA” — even though he has worn “Make American Great Again” hats at multiple public events and served as head of DOGE, the Trump administration’s ad-hoc cost-cutting department, for several months in 2025 before he exited as a “special government employee” amid a dispute with Trump.
	

	Said Musk, “I’m not sure what MAGA means” but “if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party then I certainly don’t have that. I think there are positives and negatives in both parties… but politics is very tribal. A lot of people cannot see any good in the other party, and they cannot see any bad in their own party because they’re more or less invested in their party like it’s their hometown sports team, and it’s just their team, and they won’t accept that there’s anything that the other team can do that’s good or anything that their team can do that’s bad.”

	Musk last month said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a potential merger. “There’s more and more areas of interaction or overlap with SpaceX and Tesla that that didn’t exist before,” he said at the DealBook conference. “So if you’d asked me five years ago, do I ever think there’s any purpose in SpaceX and Tesla getting together? I would have said ‘no.’” He continued, “really, it’s just a question of do SpaceX and Tesla execute better together and create more value than if they’re apart… and that would be up to the shareholders to decide.”

	Musk also spoke about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation last week, after the revelation that he had engaged in several affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and an Nvidia employee. Musk, who has suggested Huang be reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO, said Haung’s removal as chief executive of the AI company was like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team,” while also acknowledging that Huang “certainly made some mistakes.”

	Musk, interviewed by the New York Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin, discussed the controversy over Starlink’s recent restrictions on satellite internet access to the Ukrainian military amid the war being waged on the country by Russia. Musk said, “From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system. It is not meant to to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people…. If you want to do that you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the U.S. government, but do not ask me as as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives, not just soldiers.”

	Musk appeared at the DealBook conference in 2023, where he accused advertisers who had pulled ads from X over his support of an antisemitic conspiracy theory of “blackmail” and told them — calling out Bob Iger, then CEO of Disney, by name — to “Go fuck yourself.”

title: Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama ‘The Traveler,’ Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Chris Pratt is setting up his next sci-fi adventure: starring in Paramount Pictures‘ big-screen adaptation of “The Traveler,” based on the novel by
body:
Chris Pratt is setting up his next sci-fi adventure: starring in Paramount Pictures‘ big-screen adaptation of “The Traveler,” based on the novel by Joseph Eckert.

	The film is part of the new first-look, three-year producing deal Pratt inked at the studio through his Indivisible Productions banner. Pratt will potentially star in select projects. 

	Eckert’s “The Traveler” tells the story of a reluctant time traveler and his son, and “the bond between them that even millennia cannot break.” A synopsis describes the story as “an adventure full of heartbreak, hope and futures beyond imagination.” Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein will direct “The Traveler,” based on a screenplay by Justin Rhodes. The film will be produced by Adam Rosenberg and Jules Daly. 
	

	Additional projects under Pratt’s deal include “Miami Heat,” written by Brad Copeland (“Jerry & Marge Go Large”), with Pratt set to star and produce alongside Hutch Parker (“Venom: The Last Dance”).

	Notably, Pratt was among the superstars featured in Paramount’s CinemaCon reel this spring, as David Ellison unveiled his vision for the movie studio under the Skydance umbrella. (Pratt appears in a scene in the executive dining room with director Jon M. Chu, Molly Ringwald, Miles Teller, Damson Idris, Isabel May, Will Smith and James Wan.)

	It’s no surprise that Paramount wanted to get in the Pratt business, since it stands to be quite profitable for all parties. The actor has earned more than $15 billion at the worldwide box office, including starring roles in Marvel’s “Guardians of the Galaxy” trilogy and “Avengers” movies, as well as Universal’s “Jurassic World” series and as the voice of Mario in the blockbuster “Super Mario Bros.” movies. (The most recent film, “The Super Mario Bros. Galaxy” movie debuted in April and has grossed over $1 billion globally.) Up next, Pratt produced and stars in “Way of the Warrior Kid” for Apple TV. The film, which adapts Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel, launches on Nov. 25.
	

	After starting his career on TV with shows like “Parks and Recreation” and “Everwood,” Pratt returned in 2022 with the hit series “The Terminal List,” which streams on Amazon’s Prime Video. Pratt produces and stars in the show; the second season, subtitled “True Believer,” debuted on the streamer last month.

title: Why ‘GTA’ Has Never Been Adapted for Film or TV: ‘We Prefer to Control Our Own Destiny,’ Take-Two CEO Says
description: With this week’s debut of “Grand Theft Auto 6” widely considered to be the entertainment event of the decade, the Rockstar Games-created franchise
body:
With this week’s debut of “Grand Theft Auto 6” widely considered to be the entertainment event of the decade, the Rockstar Games-created franchise seems like an obvious target for a Hollywood adaptation. But those producers hoping to land the rights could be waiting indefinitely, as Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has said for years that the company is not interested.

	“We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment we’re always proud of,” Zelnick said in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show Nov. 12. “We would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that. And of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.”
	

	Zelnick isn’t being coy here, as he’s provided the same answer for years now when asked about the possibility of adapting “GTA” for film or TV. In August 2024, the Take-Two Interactive told Variety the Rockstar Games owner has “selectively licensed intellectual properties” and “the value of those licenses is typically not all that significant, even in great success.”

	Beginning with its first title released in 1997, Rockstar Games’ “Grand Theft Auto” franchise is comprised of six mainline titles, as of the release of “GTA 6” on Friday. The games are known for their M rating, extreme violence and criminal activity, largely in the form of committing grand theft auto. For “GTA 6,” the franchise is pushing the boundaries of the open-world genre with the immersive story of Jason and Lucia, a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style criminal duo running on the streets of the fictional Vice City.
	

	In November 2024, Zelnick used the box-office bomb that was the “Borderlands” movie (which was developed and filmed prior to Take-Two’s acquisition of “Borderlands” game studio Gearbox) as an example of what could go wrong if the company’s IP, including “GTA,” was adapted for another medium.

	“While the ‘Borderlands’ movie was indeed disappointing, it was good for our catalog sales of the ‘Borderlands’ titles,” Zelnick told Variety. “So we would prefer to have a huge hit and, as you know, we didn’t have a financial exposure to the negative [on the ‘Borderlands’ movie]. So we are selective for exactly the reason that you just cannot control these outcomes and we prefer to control our own destiny. However, we still will license selectively.”

	Zelnick hasn’t ruled it out, but sources tell Variety that the team at Rockstar Games, which has also produced the hit “Red Dead Redemption” franchise, is more focused on continuing to build on the “GTA” world within gaming rather than adapting it for Hollywood. The plan has worked out so far: “GTA 6″ currently has a 99 score on Metacritic ahead of its Thursday release, tying it for the highest-rated video game of all time.

schema.headline: Why ‘GTA’ Has Never Been Adapted for Film or TV: ‘We Prefer to Control Our Own Destiny,’ Take-Two CEO Says

title: Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux to Star in ‘Sleepover’ From Blumhouse Atomic and Universal
description: Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux are set to star in “Sleepover” from Blumhouse Atomic and Universal Pictures. The horror movie is set for theat
body:
Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux are set to star in “Sleepover” from Blumhouse Atomic and Universal Pictures. The horror movie is set for theatrical release on Oct. 8, 2027.

	“Insidious: Out of the Further” filmmaker Jacob Chase is directing the project from a script he co-wrote with “Night Swim” screenwriter Bryce McGuire. “Sleepover” is based on McGuire’s original short story. Plot details and further casting remain under wraps. 
	

	Variety exclusively reported in October that Parker Posey was set to star in “Sleepover,” but she has since dropped out of the project. Monaghan was cast in her place. Posey revealed the exit during a recent “Today” interview. When asked about the project, she told Craig Melvin, “I’m not doing it anymore … Something came up.” 

	Monaghan, known for roles in films like “Kiss Kiss Bang Bang,” “Source Code” and “Gone Baby Gone,” most recently starred alongside Robert De Niro and Adam Scott in the Netflix crime thriller “The Whisper Man.” Also for Netflix, she appeared in the buddy comedy “Little Brother” with John Cena and Eric Andre. On the horizon for Monaghan is Netflix’s hockey drama series “The Sticks,” which also stars Emilie Bierre and Shai Chase, and the third season of Apple TV’s “Your Friends and Neighbors.”

	Theroux is no stranger to the horror genre. One of his best-known roles was playing the scorned movie exec Adam in David Lynch’s twisty masterpiece “Mulholland Drive.” More recently, he starred in “Beetlejuice Beetlejuice” as the manipulative TV producer boyfriend of Winona Ryder’s Lydia Deetz. His most recent big-screen credit was for “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” On the TV side, Theroux last starred in Netflix’s sports comedy “Running Point” and played the iconic post-apocalyptic capitalist Robert House in Prime Video’s “Fallout.” Upcoming projects for Theroux include “The Billion Dollar Spy” with Russell Crowe and Apple TV’s Siegfried and Roy miniseries “Wild Things.” 
	

	“Sleepover” reunites Chase and Blumhouse Atomic after “Out of the Further.” The sixth installment in the “Insidious” franchise opened in August to $60 million worldwide and went on to gross $169 million against an $18 million budget.

	Jason Blum serves as producer. Chase and McGuire serve as executive producers, with Bea Sequeira serving as executive producer for Blumhouse and Lilly Tyson overseeing the project for the company. “Sleepover” is a Cinescape Entertainment production, presented by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic.

	Monaghan is represented by Gersh, Anonymous Content, Entertainment 360, Narrative and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. Theroux is represented by CAA, Lighthouse Management & Media, Ingenuity Group and Toczek Suddleson Law Group.

title: As U.S. Infrastructure Crumbles, ABC’s ‘World News Tonight’ Posts Highest Week-Long Daily Ratings Since COVID
description: A week after the midterm elections generated tremendous audiences for the network evening newscasts, last week’s unpredictable string of news — inc
body:
A week after the midterm elections generated tremendous audiences for the network evening newscasts, last week’s unpredictable string of news — including the Microsoft Outlook blackout, followed by the nationwide grounding of air flights — propelled ABC’s “World News Tonight” to heights the telecast hasn’t seen in years.

	The busy news week also included the Nvidia scandal, the Brooklyn building collapse, the Pete Hegseth impeachment vote, fallout from the midterm elections (and late-breaking results like Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom) and more.
	

	According to ABC News, “World News Tonight” averaged more than 9 million Total Viewers on each of its five telecasts last week — the first time it has done that in nearly six years, during the COVID era (specifically, the week of Feb. 15, 2021). 

	“Audiences are turning to ‘World News Tonight with David Muir’ in numbers we haven’t seen since the COVID pandemic, a powerful reflection of the trust they place in our journalism during uncertain times,” said ABC News president Almin Karamehmedovic in a statement to Variety. “Amid a relentless week of breaking news, culminating in Friday’s nationwide ground stop, more than 9 million Americans tuned in every single night. We are deeply grateful for their confidence and never take that responsibility for granted.”

	Over the entire week (except for Monday, which wasn’t included due to Monday Night Football), “World News Tonight with David Muir” was No. 1 with total viewers (9.251 million) on all of broadcast and cable (excluding sports) for the second week in a row and landed its best number in four years, according to Nielsen’s Live+Same Day Big Data Plus Panel Program Ratings.“World News Tonight with David Muir” was also No. 1 with adults 25-54 (1.366 million) and adults 18-49 (993,000). In comparison, “NBC Nightly News” averaged 7.117 million total viewers, 1.161 million with adults 25-54 and 849,000 with adults 18-49, while “CBS Evening News” averaged 4.633 million viewers, 689,000 with adults 25-54 and 527,000 among adults 18-49.
	

	Season to date, “World News Tonight” is up 14% year-to-year in total viewers (8.679 million vs. 7.586 million), up 34% with adults 25-54 (1.214 million vs. 907,000) and up 40% with adults 18-49 (883,000 vs. 629,000), based on Most Current Big Data+Panel Ratings. ABC notes that “World News Tonight” is posting its best ratings since the 2020-2021 season and that its total viewers lead over “NBC Nightly News” is its largest advantage in 32 years, and its lead over “CBS Evening News” is its largest advantage in at least 35 years.

schema.headline: As U.S. Infrastructure Crumbles, ABC’s ‘World News Tonight’ Posts Highest Week-Long Daily Ratings Since COVID

title: Pierce Brosnan Welcomes Robert Pattinson Into the James Bond Family: ‘You Are Going to Be Magnificent’
description: Pierce Brosnan, a former James Bond himself, has taken to social media to enthusiastically endorse the newly anointed Robert Pattinson, who was ann
body:
Pierce Brosnan, a former James Bond himself, has taken to social media to enthusiastically endorse the newly anointed Robert Pattinson, who was announced as the new 007 on Monday. 

	“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan, who played the character in four films from 1995 to 2002, wrote on Instagram Wednesday. “You are going to be magnificent. I have fond memories of our time together making ‘Remember Me.’ It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride. Grá mor, Pierce.”
	

	As the “Parent Trap” actor noted in his caption, the two stars first worked together on 2010’s “Remember Me,” a romantic drama also starring Emilie de Ravin and Meghan Markle. With his statement, Brosnan joins stars including Pattinson’s “Tenet” co-star Elizabeth Debicki and former Bond villain Rami Malek in congratulating the “Twilight” actor on securing the role. 

	Pattinson’s announcement as the next Bond put an end to long-swirling rumors surrounding which actor would step into the role. Other stars in the mix included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, Tom Francis, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Harris Dickinson and even Harry Styles. Denis Villeneuve will direct the forthcoming film from Amazon MGM.

	Before the casting news broke, Brosnan told The Times in September that he thought the new James Bond would be “someone that none of us know about.” He had also noted that “there are lots of good hats in the ring” and “lots of great actors” being considered. When it came to names, Brosnan remained neutral: “I wouldn’t pick anyone,” he continued. “My wife told me not to say anything, and I’ve said too much. Because once I say something it goes [everywhere] and I get hanged.”

schema.headline: Pierce Brosnan Welcomes Robert Pattinson Into the James Bond Family: ‘You Are Going to Be Magnificent’

body:

		The Next Bond Theme: From Taylor Swift to Raye, 16 Singers Who Could Croon for Robert Pattinson’s 007
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Collage: Variety; Photos: GettyImages; Background: Adobe Stock
	

		
	
				

	The James Bond films are filled with traditions: the martinis are shaken, not stirred; the tuxes are immaculately tailored; the women are gorgeous; the villains are fascinating. Importantly, the films wouldn’t be true Bond stories without a dramatic theme song written and performed by a star. Nancy Sinatra, Shirley Bassey, Paul McCartney & Wings, Madonna, Jack White and Adele are just some of the acts who have brought soaring anthems to the films’ introductions. With Robert Pattinson’s Bond just announced, it’s prime time to dreamcast a new singer for the new film. Check out Variety‘s top picks below.


			
			
	Marc Anthony
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	Many Bond numbers are heavy on brass and horns. Insert Marc Anthony, who can make any song feel cinematic. In 2024, Lin-Manuel Miranda penned an op-ed for Variety calling the 58-year-old the Latino community’s Frank Sinatra, writing: “He is our Sinatra and when we hear him, we also hear the echoes of all the unforgettable moments in our own lives.” The salsa king will have his “The Last Dance World Tour” in 2027, so perhaps he can fit in a nice writing credit to bring some excitement to the new iteration of 007? Let’s give him a sweeping bilingual ballad about loving someone who’s going to betray you, and the audience will melt in their seats. — C.D.
		
			
			
	Bad Bunny
			
										
					Image Credit: Greg Swales for Variety				
					
				
	Bond can always use some Latin flavor! Who wouldn’t be more iconic than the biggest artist on the planet? Bad Bunny already conquered the Super Bowl, and his album “DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOTOS” became the first fully Spanish-language album to win the Grammy for album of the year. The Puerto Rican superstar already has a bit of assassin experience with his scene-stealing turn in the film “Bullet Train.” Can you imagine a moody, reggaeton-laced theme in Spanish playing over the opening titles, followed by a revolutionary performance on the Oscars telecast? A global event, indeed. — C.D.
		
			
			
	Beyoncé
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner/Billboard				
					
				
	The Queen can do no wrong. Beyoncé already has some experience in the spy business, having played Foxxy Cleopatra in “Austin Powers in Goldmember.” Now it’s time for her to take on the real deal. Fresh off winning Album of the Year at the 2025 Grammys for “Cowboy Carter,” and with two Oscar-nominated songs to her credit— “Listen” from “Dreamgirls” and “Be Alive” from “King Richard” — expectations would be sky-high. A Tina Turner-inspired Bond theme, complete with powerhouse vocals and a rock-and-soul edge, could be the perfect way to usher in a new era of 007. — C.D.
		
			
			
	Mariah Carey
			
										
					Image Credit: Ethan James Green				
					
				
	Do we remember the Winter Olympics in Milan? That soaring high note on the Italian classic “Volare” reminded us that Mariah Carey still has it, and it’s almost criminal that she hasn’t conquered this kingdom yet. That five-octave range is tailor-made for an iconic Bond finale: the orchestra drops out, the tension builds, and Mariah unleashes one final, earth-shattering note on a slow-burning ballad. Give us Mariah! — C.D.
		
			
			
	Olivia Dean
			
										
					Image Credit: Gilbert Flores/Billboard				
					
				
	The Bond universe isn’t averse to fresh blood when it comes to picking artists for theme songs (see: Billie Eilish and Adele), so it’s not entirely out of the realm of possibility that Olivia Dean could be tapped to record an original for the new Bond film. She’s got the range and poise that live up to the most classic of Bond themes, plus her British pedigree suits her cleanly for the role. Put her in the studio with an orchestra and you’ve got yourself a formula for Bond magic. — S.H.
		
			
			
	Lana Del Rey
			
										
					Image Credit: Gilbert Flores/Billboard				
					
				
	Few artists make more sense to record a Bond theme than Lana Del Rey, whose sweeping ballads and cinematic songwriting scream 007. And it would be something of a redemptive arc for her, considering that she previously revealed that she had penned and recorded the song “24” from her “Honeymoon” album for “Spectre,” only for Sam Smith to get the job. Del Rey has since inched closer to Bond glory earlier this year with “First Light,” the theme for the video game “007 First Light,” but the big ticket is just out of reach. — S.H.
		
			
			
	Cynthia Erivo
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner/Variety				
					
				
	Earlier this year, Cynthia Erivo performed at the Hollywood Bowl and delivered a remarkable rendition of Gladys Knight’s “Licence to Kill” from the James Bond film of the same name. Dear Denis Villeneuve and the Bond producers: you must watch the performance on YouTube and consider Erivo. She’s perfectly British, and her vocals are elegant, soulful and filled with grandeur. She also has a cinematic style and would be a perfect entry into the Bond franchise. — J.T.
		
			
			
	Celine Dion
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	The Canadian chanteuse is back in the public eye after struggling with health issues, and who better to deliver a soaring anthem that unites the world? She’s no stranger to the genre, delivering gems such as the indelible “My Heart Will Go On” for “Titanic” and the underrated “Ashes” for “Deadpool 2.” Plus her powerful four octave range is sure to match the intensity of any orchestra she’s singing alongside. Step aside and let Dion put the “power” in “power ballad.”   — W.E. 
		
			
			
	Lady Gaga
			
										
					Image Credit: Variety				
					
				
	Lady Gaga knows how to write music for film. She won an Oscar for “Shallow” from “A Star Is Born,” and she wrote “Harlequin,” an album inspired by her “Joker: Folie à Deux” character Harley Quinn. This week, she landed two Grammy nominations for “Runway,” from “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” She also has the vocal range to deliver jazz standards, as displayed during her Las Vegas Residency, “Jazz and Piano.” Gaga checks the boxes to write a soaring classic 007 theme. — J.T.
		
			
			
			
										
					Image Credit: Rich Polk/Billboard				
					
				
	Raye, who was recently named Variety’s 2026 Hitmaker of the Year, is one of music’s hottest stars. And yet her voice has a timeless quality which would certainly speak to old-school Bond fans who are looking for a more classically-sounding theme. Plus, her smoky vocals can stand alongside complex arringements, which come with the territory on Bond songs. Plus, she has the secret agent bona fides down, as she’s best known for solving a mystery … after all, where the hell is her husband? — W.E.
		
			
			
	Rosalía
			
										
					Image Credit: Beth Savaro				
					
				
	We already have a James Bond theme song preview from Rosalía if anyone has listened to “Lux,” her fourth studio album, where she sings in 13 languages, paired with operatic vocals and a thundering choice with Björk. The Spanish-born pop star is incredibly hot at the moment, as shown by pulling in nine Grammy nominations this year and a résumé that includes 13 number-one hits. She can bring the drama, the intrigue and a little flamenco flair to the next 007 adventure. — C.D.
		
			
			
	Sienna Spiro
			
										
					Image Credit: Variety 				
					
				
	She’s not quite the superstar, yet, that virtually all the others on this list are, but she’s certainly on or approaching that bubble. That the British upstart styles herself like someone right out of a ’60s swinging-London film helps set the mood for thinking of her as a Bond girl: You could visually picture her silhouette fitting right into the title sequence, without having to hire a ringer. But it’s not so much about her nostalgic look — it’s that voice, which one of her obvious inspirations, former Bond theme-stress Adele, has cosigned. The most obvious sign it could or should be Spiro: one great song on her new album, called “Time, You and Me,” already sounds like a classic Bond theme. If it were, it’d be one of the two or three best 007 songs this century. Spiro could surely find another one where that came from. — C.W.
		
			
			
	Harry Styles
			
										
					Image Credit: Zak Hussein/Billboard				
					
				
	Harry Styles would be the perfect candidate to write the new James Bond theme. Having gone from One Direction breakout to a hugely successful solo performer, Styles can deliver both pop and rock with strong vocals. He also co-wrote the Bleachers song “Alfie’s Song (Not So Typical Love Song)” for the 2018 film “Love, Simon,” but that was more of a pop bop. Think instead of 2017’s “Sign of the Times.” The song is a perfect power ballad. For Bond, Styles would be matched with a large orchestra. And despite a screen test, if he can’t get to play James Bond, delivering a Bond song for the franchise would be the next best thing. — J.T.
		
			
			
	Taylor Swift
			
										
					Image Credit: Gilbert Flores/Variety				
					
				
	Hiring an A-list Bond? Consider an A-list superstar to do the theme. Swift is certainly ambitious enough to consider doing a 007 song, an elite club of music’s best and brightest. She’s certainly open to writing for films, as her current hit “I Knew It, I Knew You” is from “Toy Story 5” — and she’s already hitting the promotional trail to ensure it gets ample Oscar consideration. But we know she could have an interesting take on the drama, intrigue and romance that fuels every Bond song … after all, her catalogue is filled with big emotions. — W.E.
		
			
			
	Suki Waterhouse
			
										
					Image Credit: Zoe McConnell for Variety				
					
				
	Sure, there’s novelty in getting Pattinson’s longtime fiancée in the mix to sing his theme song. But Waterhouse is a respected musician with three albums and plenty of touring under her belt, and a sultry alto that adds texture to her indie rock hits. Her most recent album, “Loveland” has some complex arrangements, and she’s still able to hold her own, which is necessary as the inevitable Bond theme orchestra swells. Hell, while we’re at it, make her a Bond Girl, too, and tickets will sell like crazy. — W.E.
		
			
			
	Hayley Williams
			
										
					Image Credit: Rolling Stone				
					
				
	The Paramore belter has shown, between her band’s genre experimentation and her own freewheeling solo material, that she’s not constrained by sound. Although 007-style bombast would be yet another gear, it’d be fascinating for to try that style on for size. Besides, the Villeneuve Bond will inevitably be edgy: Williams is the perfect choice to bring some grit to the secret agent glam. Besides, Pattinson ushered in an era of the emo Batman … could an emo Bond be next? If so, who better than Williams to sing his feelings! — W.E.
		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

title: 'Reasonable Doubt' Emayatzy Corinealdi's Ex-Nanny Claims She Was Fired After Asking For Overtime Pay
description:
'Reasonable Doubt' Star Sued
                          You Fired Me When I Tried To Collect My Un
body:
'Reasonable Doubt' Star Sued
                          You Fired Me When I Tried To Collect My Unpaid OT
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Emayatzy Corinealdi -- the star of "Reasonable Doubt" -- is being sued by a former nanny who claims she was fired after asking about unpaid overtime she says she was owed ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
              In court docs, obtained by TMZ, Shaniqua Wolfe's attorneys claim she was initially hired at $30 per hour, overtime at $45 per hour, and 70 cents per mile for gas reimbursement to work for Emayatzy.
      
    
              Wolfe claims she worked around 54 hours a week during her first month and says she basically worked as Emayatzy's personal assistant, as opposed to just a nanny.
      

              Per the docs, Wolfe claims that though she worked a total of roughly 120.42 hours in a two-week period, she only received $2,426.66 of the $4,218.90 she says she was owed per the regular and overtime rates.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Wolfe says after she asked Emayatzy how to request the overtime, Emayatzy responded, "You feel like there's been a lot of overtime? I thought it evened out with the later days in the week."
      
    
              Wolfe claims Emayatzy promised a better system but then deducted 14.5 hours from Wolfe's pay without itemized proof ... claiming that it was owed for time spent at chiropractor appointments in April.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              In July, Wolfe says she submitted an overtime request and claims Emayatzy promised to pay it ... but Wolfe says when she followed up two days later, Emayatzy fired her the very next day.
      
    
              Wolfe is now seeking unpaid overtime and mileage reimbursement ... but also damages for emotional distress and attorneys' fees.

title: Dolly Parton’s Niece Honors Late Singer at CMAs with Custom Dress
description:
Dolly Parton
                          Niece Honors Late Singer in Custom Dress at CMAs
body:
Dolly Parton
                          Niece Honors Late Singer in Custom Dress at CMAs
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 18, 2026
                            5:25 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Dolly Parton’s niece brought a personal piece of the country legend to the CMA Awards ... stepping onto the red carpet in an outfit originally created for her late aunt.
      
    
              Danielle Parton attended Wednesday’s ceremony in Nashville wearing a white, long-sleeved dress with gold embellishments and sparkling fringe ... finishing the look with metallic gold boots. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              And the story behind the sparkle made the outfit even more special ... Danielle told Taste of Country ahead of the show the dress was made for Dolly for “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” which recently earned a Grammy nomination.
      
    
              According to Danielle, Dolly had tried it on, but never got to wear it for its intended occasion. Her niece decided the CMAs would be the perfect opportunity to give it a meaningful debut. 
      
    
              Speaking to On the Red Carpet, Danielle credited Dolly’s longtime costume designer Steve Summers with creating the outfit ... joking, “they poured me into it tonight,” before explaining she wanted to honor her aunt by wearing it. 
      
    
              The tribute comes after Dolly died in August at 80. Danielle was named brand ambassador for her aunt’s estate last month ... taking on a public role in helping preserve her legacy.
      
    
              A little family history ... and a whole lot of Dolly sparkle.

title: 'You' Actor Alexander Haskin Slapped Woman Before Drowning Off Santa Monica Pier
description:
'You' Actor Alexander Haskin
                          Slapped Woman Before Jumping Off Pier, Dro
body:
'You' Actor Alexander Haskin
                          Slapped Woman Before Jumping Off Pier, Drowning
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              Alexander Haskin -- who appeared on Netflix's "You" -- has been identified as the man who slapped a woman before jumping off the Santa Monica pier and dying in the ocean.
      
    
              Witnesses said that the man, later ID'd as the 38-year-old Netflix actor, was in an argument with the woman he slapped before jumping over the pier railings ... the California Post reported.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              Haskin's father, Dana, is a California Highway Patrol officer, and he told the outlet that his son didn't appear distressed before the incident ... and he has no idea why his son jumped. He also didn't know who the woman was.
      

              Dana said ... "In the heat of the moment, who knows what a human brain can do? It's still a big mystery to us … we keep asking why."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
              Officers responded to reports that Haskin had jumped off the pier around 4:06 PM PT Monday ... 50 minutes later, they were pulling his body from the water.
      
    
              Haskin was later identified by the L.A. County Medical Examiner ... with his cause of death deferred.
      
    
              In addition to "You," Haskin -- who was also a personal trainer -- made appearances in "The Rookie" and "Mayans M.C."
      
    
              RIP
